claims.claim_text: Cultural canons are manufactured by money and luck amplifying exposure, with quality only a loose filter.
claims.evidence_quote: Quality acts as a loose filter... the vast middle ground... is dominated by capital and luck.
claims.reasoning: SOURCE states quality is a loose filter and capital/luck dominate the middle, matching the summary.

claims.claim_text: We remember fewer than 20 of 200 to 500 Viennese contemporaries and 3,400 catalogued composers.
claims.evidence_quote: between 200 and 500 active composers... IMSLP catalogs over 3,400 composers... We remember fewer than 20.
claims.reasoning: All counts and the under-20 figure match SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: The question is patronage and access, not only merit.
claims.evidence_quote: Or were they the ones who happened to have the right patron, the right court position, the right access...
claims.reasoning: Captures the author's open question about patronage versus merit.

claims.claim_text: History cannot rerun, but a model of cultural markets can run thousands of times.
claims.evidence_quote: We can't rewind history... But we can build a model of cultural markets and run that thousands of times.
claims.reasoning: Near-verbatim restatement of the source sentence.

claims.claim_text: Opening question: was Bach his era's Bieber, and will Bieber be our era's Bach?
claims.evidence_quote: whether Bach was the Justin Bieber of his time... will people 300 years from now be listening to Bieber and think that was the best we had to offer?
claims.reasoning: Rephrases both halves of the opening question with equivalent meaning.

claims.claim_text: Three hypotheses compete: cream rises, money writes, floors and ceilings.
claims.evidence_quote: I set up the project to test three competing hypotheses.
claims.reasoning: Matches the three named stories in SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: Cream Rises: over long horizons quality wins; replayed history keeps roughly the same canon.
claims.evidence_quote: over long enough time horizons, genuine quality wins... you'd end up with roughly the same canon.
claims.reasoning: Direct restatement of Story 1.

claims.claim_text: Money Writes History: who gets heard first wins; quality is almost irrelevant.
claims.evidence_quote: success is mostly about who gets heard first... Quality is almost irrelevant.
claims.reasoning: Matches Story 2 wording closely.

claims.claim_text: Floors and Ceilings: extremes are predictable, but the vast middle depends on luck and money.
claims.evidence_quote: The truly terrible never succeed... the truly transcendent sometimes break through. But for the vast majority in the middle... depends on luck, money, and timing.
claims.reasoning: Faithful compression of Story 3.

claims.claim_text: Job analogy: among twenty pretty-good candidates, hiring turns on luck and timing.
claims.evidence_quote: among the twenty 'pretty good' candidates, who gets hired often comes down to who knew someone...
claims.reasoning: Preserves the analogy and the twenty-candidate figure.

claims.claim_text: Three documented mechanisms combine: mere exposure, social influence, cumulative advantage.
claims.evidence_quote: The model incorporates three phenomena that are individually well-documented in psychology and economics...
claims.reasoning: Matches the three named mechanisms.

claims.claim_text: Mere exposure (Zajonc 1968; Bornstein 1989, 208 experiments, r = 0.26) peaks then reverses.
claims.evidence_quote: Zajonc demonstrated this in 1968, and Bornstein's 1989 meta-analysis across 208 experiments... r = 0.26. The effect peaks at moderate exposure and reverses with overexposure.
claims.reasoning: All years, counts, effect size, and curve shape match SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: Extra airtime creates artificial quality advantage; money-driven exposure contaminates judging.
claims.evidence_quote: artists who get more initial airtime develop an artificial quality advantage... the judging is contaminated by the exposure, and the exposure was determined by money.
claims.reasoning: Direct restatement of the causal claim.

claims.claim_text: Salganik MusicLab (2006): 14,341 listeners, 48 songs; same song ranked 1st or 40th.
claims.evidence_quote: Salganik MusicLab experiment (2006)... 14,341 participants could listen to 48 unknown songs... rank 1st... and 40th.
claims.reasoning: All figures and the ranking range match SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: Matthew effect magnifies small differences; court at 20 beats missing by one year.
claims.evidence_quote: Merton called this the Matthew Effect. Small initial differences... get magnified... a court position at age 20... missed that appointment by one year never gets to build.
claims.reasoning: Preserves attribution and the age-20 example.

claims.claim_text: Producers get uncorrelated quality and capital; consumers add exposure and social signals; success feeds back.
claims.evidence_quote: Quality and capital are uncorrelated... Consumers form opinions based on actual quality plus the mere exposure effect plus social signals. Success feeds back into more exposure.
claims.reasoning: Faithful summary of the model setup.

claims.claim_text: Runs of 1,000 producers and 10,000 consumers, about 2 minutes each, 360+ per condition.
claims.evidence_quote: Each run takes about two minutes with 1,000 producers and 10,000 consumers... ran 360+ per condition.
claims.reasoning: All numeric values match SOURCE exactly.

claims.claim_text: Author built a simulation; formal paper linked, post is the informal version.
claims.evidence_quote: I built a simulation to find out. The full technical paper is here... This post is the less formal version.
claims.reasoning: Matches the meta description of the project.

claims.claim_text: Results: influence weakens quality link; canons reshuffle; capital dominates.
claims.evidence_quote: the correlation between actual quality and commercial success drops... equalizing starting resources jumps the quality-canon correlation... Capital gates access.
claims.reasoning: Summarizes the three headline results accurately.

claims.claim_text: With social influence visible, quality-success correlation drops (p < 0.0001, 360 runs).
claims.evidence_quote: the quality-success correlation drops significantly (p < 0.0001 across 360 runs per condition).
claims.reasoning: p-value and run count match SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: Charts and view counts push away from independent judgment via proxy optimization.
claims.evidence_quote: Every 'Top 40' chart... pushes us away from independent judgment. We use popularity as a proxy for quality, then optimize for the proxy.
claims.reasoning: Preserves the proxy-contamination argument.

claims.claim_text: Talent constant over 200 runs; reshuffled resources yield counterfactual distance 0.88 of 1.
claims.evidence_quote: I ran it 200 times. The counterfactual distance was 0.88 on a 0-to-1 scale.
claims.reasoning: Run count and distance value match SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: Only top 10% have a shot regardless of funding, even then only about 1 in 4; 50th to 90th faces lottery.
claims.evidence_quote: Only the top 10% of talent had a meaningful shot... only about 1 in 4. For everyone in the 50th to 90th percentile... effectively a lottery.
claims.reasoning: Percentages and 1-in-4 figure match; minor drop of 'meaningful' preserves sense.

claims.claim_text: Full model 0.32; no social influence 0.35; equal capital 0.46; quality only 0.46: equalizing adds 44%.
claims.evidence_quote: Full model... 0.32; No social influence... 0.35; Equal capital... 0.46; Quality only... 0.46... jumps the quality-canon correlation by 44%.
claims.reasoning: Every correlation and the 44% figure match SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: Stylized 1750 Vienna, 300 composers: distance 0.97, only 2.5 percent shared between histories.
claims.evidence_quote: rewind to 1750... 300 composers... counterfactual distance was 0.97... Only 2.5% of canonical composers were shared.
claims.reasoning: Year, count, distance, and 2.5% match SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: Varying parameters ±50%: steep money-to-attention conversion sidelines quality.
claims.evidence_quote: I varied every parameter by ±50%. The single most important factor is how steeply money converts into attention... quality barely matters.
claims.reasoning: Preserves the ±50% range and convex-conversion conclusion.

claims.claim_text: Major-label placement reaching 50 million versus independent self-promotion reaching 500.
claims.evidence_quote: major label can buy a front-page Spotify placement reaching 50 million listeners while an independent artist's self-promotion reaches 500.
claims.reasoning: Both figures and the comparison match SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: Quality sets a floor and a ceiling; the middle is capital and luck.
claims.evidence_quote: It sets a floor below which you can't succeed and a ceiling above which you probably will. But the vast middle ground... is dominated by capital and luck.
claims.reasoning: Direct restatement of the Story 3 conclusion.

claims.claim_text: Bach may be greatest only among those resourced to be heard, published, preserved.
claims.evidence_quote: Bach is the greatest composer who ever lived among those who had the resources to be heard, published, and preserved.
claims.reasoning: Matches SOURCE's qualified restatement; 'may be' is a harmless hedge.

claims.claim_text: Mechanisms run stronger today: patronage took decades, playlist placement takes hours.
claims.evidence_quote: The mechanisms are stronger today, not weaker... patronage decision played out over decades. A Spotify playlist placement plays out in hours.
claims.reasoning: Preserves the stronger-today claim and the two timescales.

claims.claim_text: Leverage is wider exposure; 1970s-80s blind auditions lifted women hires from 5% to 25%.
claims.evidence_quote: Blind auditions for orchestras, widely adopted in the 1970s-80s... the proportion of women hired by major US orchestras went from 5% to 25%.
claims.reasoning: Decade range and both percentages match SOURCE.

claims.claim_text: Canon survival proxies bestness; curricula get built on the forgotten proxy.
claims.evidence_quote: We use 'survived into the canon' as a proxy for 'was the best,' then build entire curricula... forgetting it was ever a proxy at all.
claims.reasoning: Faithful restatement of the proxy argument.

claims.claim_text: Quality as stable property is debatable; calibration leaps decades; genre and politics excluded.
claims.evidence_quote: assumes quality is a real, stable property... philosophically debatable... Generalizing to 18th-century European aristocrats... requires a leap of faith... doesn't include: genre formation... cultural politics.
claims.reasoning: Enumerates the same caveats SOURCE lists.

claims.claim_text: Bach was excellent AND positioned; reshuffled patronage yields an almost entirely different canon.
claims.evidence_quote: He was excellent AND well-positioned... Reshuffle patronage and you get an almost entirely different canon.
claims.reasoning: Source states both the excellence/positioning conjunction and the patronage reshuffle result.

claims.claim_text: Surgeon analogy: one of fifty equally skilled becomes the best via profile, talks, book.
claims.evidence_quote: the one surgeon who gets famous out of fifty equally skilled surgeons... a profile in the New York Times, which led to speaking invitations, which led to a book deal
claims.reasoning: Source gives one-of-fifty surgeon and the profile, talks, book chain.

claims.claim_text: Probably 20 to 50 equally great contemporaries stay unknown for missing the Leipzig-type job.
claims.evidence_quote: there were probably 20 to 50 of his contemporaries who were equally great, whose names we will never know, because they didn't get that job.
claims.reasoning: Numbers 20 to 50 and the cause (missing the job) match the source exactly.

claims.claim_text: If the mechanisms in this simulation are right, future canons track distribution and algorithms.
claims.evidence_quote: if the mechanisms in this simulation are right, then whoever survives into the canon of the 2000s will have more to do with who had the best distribution deals and the most favorable algorithms than with who made the best music.
claims.reasoning: Node keeps the same conditional and the same distribution/algorithm drivers.

claims.claim_text: Taste itself was manufactured: surviving canon sets what counts as beautiful.
claims.evidence_quote: our taste was manufactured along with it... The whole chain from "who got funded" to "what counts as beautiful" is more contingent
claims.reasoning: Source explicitly ties manufactured taste to what counts as beautiful.

claims.claim_text: Author honestly does not know whether Bieber survives 300 years hence.
claims.evidence_quote: whether people 300 years from now will be listening to Bieber... I honestly don't know.
claims.reasoning: Source directly states the 300-year Bieber question and the author's lack of knowledge.
